author: Nelev
body:
## What
PDFs are masked with [Presidio](https://presidio.dataprivacystack.org/) after `load_pdf`'s checks and before splitting, so neither the embeddings nor the upload's verify model see contact details or other people's names.

- New `rag_pipeline/redact.py` (`mask_pii`): replaces phone numbers, emails, NHS/NI numbers, IBANs, card and IP numbers, and other people's names with `<ENTITY_TYPE>`. A `PERSON` is masked only if it is a full name or follows a title, because the small English spaCy model otherwise tags terms like "GORD" as people.
- The patient's own name, DOB and all dates are kept: they are in the record and on every chunk's identity line, and retrieval depends on them.
- The hidden-text, DOB and surname checks still run on the raw text, which never leaves `load_pdf`. `LoadedPdf.text` (what `averify` reads) is the masked text.
- Chunk ids depend on the masked text, so `rag_pipeline.ingest` deletes the ids of the files it re-indexes first (only those files, not PDFs attached through the agent).
- `surname(record)` moves to `chunks.py` so the identity check and masking share one rule.
- Adds `presidio-analyzer`, `presidio-anonymizer` and `en_core_web_sm`; README updated.

## Known gaps
- English-only: the Italian D08 gets some ordinary words masked as `<PERSON>`. The record JSON and identity line are not masked.
- The first upload after startup pays the spaCy model load (a few seconds).
- Effect on retrieval recall is not measured yet: re-run `rag_pipeline.ingest` and the eval before relying on it.

## Checks
`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` (171 passed).
